newsStories.headline: THE BIG STORY · CPI HITS 3.4%
newsStories.dek: August inflation came in stubbornly hot, putting next week's Federal Reserve decision under even more pressure.
newsStories.body: The August Consumer Price Index rose 3.4% from a year earlier, according to coverage highlighted in today's digest. The report is the Fed's final major inflation reading before its September 16 decision, and coverage says the odds of a rate hike jumped after the release.
newsStories.takeaway: THE FED'S INFLATION PROBLEM ISN'T GOING AWAY QUIETLY.
newsStories.source: WSJ / CNBC / CBS / CNN via Sep 11 digest

newsStories.headline: WALL STREET GOES ONCHAIN · NASDAQ → KRAKEN
newsStories.dek: Nasdaq's $100 million investment in Kraken parent Payward is looking less like a crypto bet and more like market-infrastructure strategy.
newsStories.body: Nasdaq is investing $100 million in Payward as the firms work toward tokenized equities. CNBC describes the move as a bet that tokenization becomes part of the plumbing of the stock market, while Fortune frames tokenized stocks as a major Wall Street opportunity.
newsStories.takeaway: TOKENIZATION IS MOVING FROM CRYPTO PRODUCT TO MARKET INFRASTRUCTURE.

newsStories.headline: THE SEC MAY LET THE BLOCKCHAIN BE THE RECORD
newsStories.dek: A new SEC proposal could address one of tokenized securities' biggest legal headaches: who legally owns the asset.
newsStories.body: Onchain data can show who controls a token, but traditional securities law relies on official ownership records. Coverage in today's digest says a new SEC plan could allow blockchain records to serve as the legal record for tokenized securities, potentially bringing the technology and legal ownership layer closer together.
newsStories.takeaway: A TOKENIZED STOCK GETS MUCH MORE INTERESTING WHEN THE BLOCKCHAIN RECORD ACTUALLY COUNTS.

newsStories.headline: BULLSHIT OR BULLISH? · YOUR 401(K) IS BITCOIN'S NEXT WAVE
newsStories.dek: Institutional attention is shifting from whether to own crypto toward how to integrate it into retirement portfolios.
newsStories.body: Yahoo Finance highlights the possibility that retirement accounts could drive Bitcoin's next adoption wave as institutional investors focus increasingly on implementation rather than basic consideration of crypto exposure.
newsStories.takeaway: DOES BITCOIN'S NEXT LEG COME FROM BORING RETIREMENT MONEY?
newsStories.source: Yahoo Finance / Investing.com via Sep 11 digest

newsStories.headline: VISA PUTS CARD-SETTLEMENT CREDIT ONCHAIN
newsStories.dek: Visa is reportedly opening settlement data to help fintechs borrow against card receivables using blockchain-based credit tools.
newsStories.body: Coverage highlighted in today's digest describes Visa pairing traditional VisaNet settlement data with blockchain-based lending and smart-contract infrastructure. The concept turns expected card-settlement cash flows into collateral for financing.
newsStories.takeaway: THE QUIET ONCHAIN REVOLUTION MAY LOOK MORE LIKE CREDIT INFRASTRUCTURE THAN MEME COINS.
newsStories.source: CryptoSlate / Crowdfund Insider via Sep 11 digest

newsStories.headline: YOU CAN'T MAKE THIS SHIT UP · HUNTER BIDEN COIN CRATERS 98%
newsStories.dek: Another political meme coin reportedly collapsed almost immediately after launch.
newsStories.body: Business Insider reports a Hunter Biden-themed crypto token fell about 98% in a day, trading around $0.60 after its debut and quickly prompting rug-pull accusations.
points: POLITICAL MEME COINS · SAME OLD STORY
newsStories.takeaway: HOW MANY TIMES DOES THE SAME MEME-COIN MOVIE NEED TO PLAY?

newsStories.headline: QUICK HIT · CONSENSYS IS SPLITTING IN TWO
newsStories.dek: MetaMask is set to become one company while institutional infrastructure and protocols move into another.
newsStories.body: Coverage in today's digest says ConsenSys plans to split into two companies by year-end 2026: MetaMask and a separate institutional-infrastructure-focused unit that includes the Protocols Group.
newsStories.takeaway: CRYPTO'S CONSUMER WALLET AND INSTITUTIONAL STACK ARE BECOMING DIFFERENT BUSINESSES.

aiStories.headline: AI AGENTS · KEEP THE HUMAN IN CONTROL?
aiStories.dek: As autonomous agents move into real workflows, researchers and businesses are focusing on when an agent should stop and ask a human for help.
aiStories.body: Today's digest highlights Stanford research on teaching independent AI agents to ask for help, Deloitte work on redesigning human-agent operating models, and new agent infrastructure from OpenAI. The common question is no longer whether agents can act — it's how humans retain meaningful oversight when they do.
aiStories.takeaway: THE BEST AI AGENT MAY BE THE ONE THAT KNOWS WHEN NOT TO ACT.
aiStories.source: Stanford GSB / Deloitte / OpenAI via Sep 11 digest

aiStories.headline: AI DOOMSDAY CLOCK · PEOPLE ARE LISTENING NOW
aiStories.dek: Warnings that advanced AI could threaten humanity are moving from niche debate into mainstream coverage.
aiStories.body: The Washington Post and Scientific American are among the outlets highlighted today examining catastrophic AI-risk arguments and the growing attention being paid to them.
aiStories.takeaway: HAS YOUR AI-RISK NUMBER MOVED THIS WEEK?
aiStories.source: Washington Post / Scientific American via Sep 11 digest

sportsStories.headline: NFL HISTORY · 49ERS WIN IN MELBOURNE
sportsStories.body: San Francisco beat the Los Angeles Rams in the NFL's first game in Australia, played before more than 100,000 fans in Melbourne. Sky Sports reports Brock Purdy led the 49ers while Kyren Williams scored the first NFL touchdown on Australian soil.
sportsStories.takeaway: HOW GLOBAL CAN THE NFL ACTUALLY GET?
sportsStories.source: Sky Sports / 9 News Australia via Sep 11 digest

sportsStories.headline: FRIDAY FIGHT CARD · GARCIA vs BENN GETS WEIRD
sportsStories.body: Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn are in Las Vegas for their final press conference, where Garcia reportedly taunted Benn with an egg and then declined the face-off, citing his routine.
sportsStories.source: BBC / Sky Sports via Sep 11 digest

sportsStories.headline: UFC · TOPURIA COMEBACK TALK HEATS UP
sportsStories.body: Ilia Topuria could be headed toward a blockbuster UFC return, with Dana White reportedly naming two potential comeback opponents. Meanwhile, lightweight champion Justin Gaethje says Arman Tsarukyan blew his title opportunity.
sportsStories.takeaway: THE UFC'S NEXT BIG MATCHMAKING DECISION IS GETTING CROWDED.
sportsStories.source: DAZN / MMA Fighting via Sep 11 digest

sportsStories.headline: SOLHEIM CUP · DAY ONE
sportsStories.body: The 2026 Solheim Cup is underway at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands, where Team Europe is trying to regain the trophy.
sportsStories.takeaway: TEAM GOLF TAKES OVER THE WEEKEND.
sportsStories.source: Sky Sports / BBC via Sep 11 digest
